_comment: DECLARED capability table for the pinned ODRE reference implementation, bead sq-i6du2.8.
Every row is transcribed from the implementation's OWN published support tables (the
pyodre 1.0.6 project description / README, which marks each ODRL term supported or
unsupported) and, where noted, from a read of its source. Nothing here is measured by
this lane: it is the DECLARED scope used to decide which cases are comparable at all.
A case whose constructs include a term declared unsupported is reported as
OUT-OF-SCOPE-FOR-SYSTEM (the odrl-policy-bridge paper's third measure category), never
as agreement and never as a divergence.
Update procedure: bump `pinned_version`, re-transcribe, and record the run that
system: ODRE (Open Digital Rights Enforcement) — Python implementation
source: pyodre 1.0.6 published support tables (project description) + source read of pyodre/odre.py and pyodre/python_functions.py

request_model.note: `ODRE.enforce(policy)` takes no request: odrl:assignee, odrl:target and the requested action are not read when selecting rules. Request binding, where this lane performs it, is a HARNESS step and is declared as such.

notes: `odrl:count` is listed unsupported by the implementation's own table; a count-limited grant is therefore not comparable here in either direction.
`odrl:purpose` is listed unsupported; the U3 purpose-of-use corpus is out-of-scope-for-ODRE by declaration, not by measurement.

Constraint discovery reads odrl:operator / odrl:leftOperand / odrl:rightOperand directly from the rule node (pyodre/odre.py `_constraints`), so an ODRL 2.2 `odrl:constraint`-linked constraint node is outside the query's reach — see the `odre-standard-encoding-ignores-constraints` ledger entry.
